title: "Cox_Proportional_Hazard_and_Survival_Curve"
output: html_document

General Summary:

In this file, the raw data the unregulated and down regulated gene lists, clinical data as well as the relevant libraries were imported into R. Then, the data was joined together where the patient data with the Z score for each patient was combined with the clinical data. Additionally, since Xiong et al 2020 is not clear on what variation of the counts that was used to run this univariate survival analysis, what was performed here was using DESeq() variance stabilized transformation on the raw counts and those values are going to be used for the Kaplan Meier Curve and Log Rank Test analysis.


#Step 1: Import Packages, Set Pathways for Data, and Import the Upregulated and Downregulated Genes

```{r}
library(performance)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(broom)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(pheatmap)
library(DESeq2)
library(gtsummary)

#File Pathways

Figure_Export <- file.path(here(),"Figures")

Data_Import <- file.path(here(), "Data")

#Import txt files of Upregulated and Downregulated Genes

Upregulated_Genes <- read.delim(file = file.path(Data_Import,"Upregulated_Genes.txt"), header = FALSE)

Downregulated_Genes <- read.delim(file = file.path(Data_Import,"Downregulated_Genes.txt"), header = FALSE)

#Vector of all the Genes
All_Genes <- c(Upregulated_Genes, Downregulated_Genes)

All_Genes <- unlist(All_Genes)

#Import list of genes for each metric of interest that alone have a statistically significant impact on that metric (Tumor Growth, Lymph Invasion, etc)

TumorGrowthRiskGenes <- read.delim(file = file.path(Data_Import, "TumorGrowthRisk_Genes_Univariate_Model.txt"))

LymphInvasionGenes <- read.delim(file = file.path(Data_Import, "LymphGenes_Univariate_Model.txt"))

MetastasisGenes <- read.delim(file = file.path(Data_Import, "MetastasisGenes_Univariate_Model.txt"))


#Import ColData
LUAD_ColData <- readRDS(file = file.path(Data_Import,"LUAD_Coldata.rds"))

#Import the Raw Counts and use DESeq2 to run variance stabilization on the counts


LUAD_matrix <- readRDS(file = file.path(Data_Import, "LUAD_counts.rds"))

#Checking to ensure they are true
identical(LUAD_ColData$barcode, colnames(LUAD_matrix))

#Run the Variance Stabilized Transformation and save the values in the object "VST_Expression_Values"

VST_Expression_Values <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = LUAD_matrix,
                                     colData = LUAD_ColData,
                                     design = ~ definition)

VST_Expression_Values <- vst(VST_Expression_Values, blind = TRUE)

VST_Expression_Values <- as.data.frame(assay(VST_Expression_Values))

#saveRDS(VST_Values, file = file.path(Data_Import, "VST_transformed_values.rds"))

#Import Clinical Data

LUAD_CLINICAL_DATA <- readRDS(file = file.path(Data_Import,"LUAD_Clinicaldata.rds"))

LUAD_CLINICAL_DATA <- LUAD_CLINICAL_DATA %>%
  dplyr::select(submitter_id, days_to_last_follow_up, days_to_death, vital_status)
```


#Join the VST stabilized values Data and the Clinical Data

The VST stabilized data needs to be joined with the clinical data so downstream analyses, such as Kaplan Survival Curves or Cox Proportional Hazard Models, are to be performed.

```{r}
#Transposes data and forms new dataframe
VST_Expression_Values <- VST_Expression_Values %>%
  t() %>% as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(., var = "barcode") 

VST_Expression_Values <- VST_Expression_Values %>%
  mutate(patient_id = str_extract(barcode, ".{12}")) #Extracts the first 12 characters

#pivot longer
VST_Expression_Values <- VST_Expression_Values %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(barcode, patient_id), names_to = "Gene", values_to = "VST_Values")

#Add clinical data and add whether the gene is high or low expression
VST_Values_grouped <- VST_Expression_Values %>%
  group_by(Gene) %>%
  mutate(Expression_Level = if_else(VST_Values > median(VST_Values), "High","Low")) %>%
  left_join(., LUAD_CLINICAL_DATA, by = c("patient_id" = "submitter_id"))

#Calculate variables needed for survival analysis. Here is where it is noted that 0 is the value for being alive, and 1 is for being dead
Survival_matrix <- VST_Values_grouped  %>%
  mutate(time_in_months = days_to_last_follow_up / 30.41,
         deceased = if_else(vital_status == "Alive", 0, 1))

```

#Maximum Survival Differences Function

The purpose of this function is to run repeated Kaplan-Meier Survival curves for every gene in a dataset to determine which genes (alone) have a statistically significant impact on survival. This function requires that the predictor variable be "Expression_Level" where the outcome_variables would be whether the patient is deceased and the time variable in "time in months". In this case, survival should be a 0 and deceased should be 1 as well.

```{r}

Repeated_Kaplan_Meier_Curve <- function(fulldata = data,
                                          predictor_variable = "Expression_Level",
                                          time = "time_in_months",
                                          outcome = "deceased",
                                          group_metric = "symbol",
                                          units_of_time = "months"){
  
  #Extract the variables
  predictor_metric <- fulldata[[predictor_variable]]
  time_metric <- fulldata[[time]]
  outcome_metric <- fulldata[[outcome]]
  group_metric <- fulldata[[group_metric]]
  
  
  Combined_Dataset <- data.frame(predictor_metric = predictor_metric,
                                 time_metric = time_metric,
                                 outcome_metric = outcome_metric,
                                 group_metric = group_metric)
  
  ##Choose the names of the columns for the analysis
  names <-  Combined_Dataset %>% 
    survfit(Surv(time_metric, outcome_metric) ~ predictor_metric, data = .) %>%
    surv_median(fit = .)
  
  #Run a loop to calculate the median survival for each group + p value
  
  Symbols <- unique(Combined_Dataset$group_metric) 
  
  #Create an Empty Dataframe and preallocate the length
  Pvaluegraph <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 4, nrow = length(Symbols)))
  # Pvaluegraph <- matrix(ncol = 4, nrow = length(Symbols))
  
  #Run a loop to calculate the median survival for each group + p value
  
  
  for(i in 1:length(Symbols)){
    
    Gene <- Symbols[i]
    
    filtered_data <- Combined_Dataset %>% filter(group_metric == Gene)
    
    fit <- survfit(Surv(time_metric, outcome_metric) ~ predictor_metric, data = filtered_data)
    
    median <- surv_median(fit, combine = TRUE)
    
    pval <- survdiff(Surv(time_metric, outcome_metric) ~ predictor_metric, data = filtered_data)$pval
    
    new_data <- c(Gene, as.numeric(round(median[1,2],2)), as.numeric(round(median[1,3],2)), pval)
    
    Pvaluegraph[i,] <- new_data
    
  }
  #Return the combined dataframe after renaming the column
  
  colnames(Pvaluegraph) <- c("symbol", as.character(paste("Median survival in",units_of_time, "of", names[1,1])), 
                             as.character(paste("Median survival in",units_of_time, "of",names[2,1])), "p_value")
  
  return(Pvaluegraph)   
}
```

#Upregulated Genes and association for survival

Through the use of the above function, a Kaplan Meier survival curve is to be repeated for each gene that was shown to be upregulated in all 4 datasets and then filtered for the genes that have a statistically significant difference on survival of patients with low vs high expression of that protein. The second code chunk is for the downregulated genes.*The repeated Log Rank Tests were corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisions.*

```{r}
#Create Dataframe
Upregulated_Gene_Matrix <- Survival_matrix %>%
  filter(Gene %in% Upregulated_Genes$V1) %>%
  dplyr::rename("symbol" = "Gene") 

#Run the Repeated Kaplan Meier Modeling
Upregulated_Genes_Kaplan_Meier_Modeling <- Repeated_Kaplan_Meier_Curve(fulldata=Upregulated_Gene_Matrix,
                                                                         time = "time_in_months",
                                                                         predictor_variable = "Expression_Level",
                                                                         outcome = "deceased") %>%
mutate(p_adjusted = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")) %>%
filter(p_adjusted < 0.05) %>%
mutate(`Median survival in months of predictor_metric=High` = as.numeric(`Median survival in months of predictor_metric=High`),
       `Median survival in months of predictor_metric=Low` = as.numeric(`Median survival in months of predictor_metric=Low`)) %>%
mutate(Survival_Difference = `Median survival in months of predictor_metric=High` - `Median survival in months of predictor_metric=Low`)
```

#Downregulated Genes and association for survival

```{r}
#Create Dataframe
Downregulated_Gene_Matrix <- Survival_matrix %>%
  filter(Gene %in% Downregulated_Genes$V1) %>%
  dplyr::rename("symbol" = "Gene") 

#Run the Repeated Kaplan Meier Modeling
Downregulated_Genes_Kaplan_Meier_Modeling <- Repeated_Kaplan_Meier_Curve(fulldata=Downregulated_Gene_Matrix,
                                                                time = "time_in_months",
                                                                predictor_variable = "Expression_Level",
                                                                outcome = "deceased") %>%
mutate(p_adjusted = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")) %>%
filter(p_adjusted < 0.05) %>%
mutate(`Median survival in months of predictor_metric=High` = as.numeric(`Median survival in months of predictor_metric=High`),
       `Median survival in months of predictor_metric=Low` = as.numeric(`Median survival in months of predictor_metric=Low`)) %>%
mutate(Survival_Difference = `Median survival in months of predictor_metric=High` - `Median survival in months of predictor_metric=Low`)
```


#Identify Correlation Matrix

Now, a correlation matrix was obtained for the genes that were upregulated and downregulated that had statistically significant impact on survival of the patients. In these cases, there is a statistically significant difference between survival in patients

```{r}
#ggplot2 Correlation mat
Survival_matrix %>%
  dplyr::select(barcode, Gene, VST_Values) %>%
  filter(Gene %in% c(Upregulated_Genes_Kaplan_Meier_Modeling$symbol, Downregulated_Genes_Kaplan_Meier_Modeling$symbol)) %>%
  pivot_wider(data=., values_from = "VST_Values", names_from = "Gene") %>% 
  rstatix::cor_mat(-barcode) %>%
  pivot_longer(data=., cols = -(rowname), names_to = "Gene", values_to = "Coefficient") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=rowname, y = Gene, fill = Coefficient))+
  geom_tile()+
  labs(x = "Gene 1", y = "Gene 2")+
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle = -45, hjust = 0))+
  scale_fill_gradient2(high = "#E7522A", low ="#347372", mid = "white")

ggsave(filename = file.path(Figure_Export, "Impacted_Genes_on_Survival_CorrMatrix_4a.png"))

#Correlation_Plot
 Survival_matrix %>%
  dplyr::select(barcode, Gene, VST_Values) %>%
  filter(Gene %in% c(Upregulated_Genes_Kaplan_Meier_Modeling$symbol, Downregulated_Genes_Kaplan_Meier_Modeling$symbol)) %>%
  pivot_wider(data=., values_from = "VST_Values", names_from = "Gene") %>% dplyr::select(-barcode) %>%
  cor() %>%
  corrplot::corrplot()
 
 
#Distance Correlation Matrix Plot to associate genes together?
 Survival_hclust <- Survival_matrix %>%
  dplyr::select(barcode, Gene, VST_Values) %>%
  filter(Gene %in% c(Upregulated_Genes_Kaplan_Meier_Modeling$symbol, Downregulated_Genes_Kaplan_Meier_Modeling$symbol)) %>%
  dist(.) %>% 
  hclust(.)
 
plot(as.dendrogram(Survival_hclust))

pheatmap(Survival_hclust)
```

# Generate a Cox proportional Hazard Model

There is quite a bit of correlation between some of the genes taht are upregulated and downregulated and their affect on survival. Therefore, a cox proportional model will be used to identify how each gene will impact patient survival.

```{r}
#Cox Genes that are independently causing statistically significant impact on survival.
Cox_genes <- c(Upregulated_Genes_Kaplan_Meier_Modeling$symbol, Downregulated_Genes_Kaplan_Meier_Modeling$symbol)

Cox_formula <- reformulate(termlabels = Cox_genes, response = "Surv(time_in_months, deceased)")

#Create the Matrix for the COX proportional hazard analysis
Cox_Matrix <- VST_Expression_Values %>%
  filter(Gene %in% Cox_genes) %>%
  pivot_wider(data=., values_from = "VST_Values", names_from = "Gene") %>%
  left_join(., LUAD_CLINICAL_DATA, by = c("patient_id" = "submitter_id")) %>%
  mutate(time_in_months = days_to_last_follow_up / 30.41,
         deceased = if_else(vital_status == "Alive", 0, 1)) #Alive == 0 and Deceased == 1

#Run initial Master Model
Cox_Model <- coxph(formula = Cox_formula, data = Cox_Matrix)

#Look at results
Cox_Model %>%
  summary()

Cox_Model %>%
  tbl_regression(exponentiate = TRUE)

#Create Equivalent to Fig 4B indicating protective and dangerous factors as expression increases for a gene
Cox_Model %>%
  tidy() %>%
  mutate(group = if_else(estimate > 0, "Dangerous Factor", "Protective Factor")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = -log10(p.value), color = group))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), color = "black", linetype = "dashed")

#Only a handful of the genes are significant, so now we will do stepwise regression. This will start with removing each gene in order from left to right

#Genes to be removed

Genes_removed <- c("CCNB2", "PRC1", "MELK","IL7R","CACNA2D2", "HSD17B6","ASPM", "ABCA8","ARHGEF6")

#Genes_Left
Cox_genes_filtered <- Cox_genes[!Cox_genes %in% Genes_removed]

#Create Formula including all of these models
Cox_formula_filtered <- reformulate(Cox_genes_filtered, response = "Surv(time_in_months, deceased)")

#Cox Model that has been identified by backwards stepwise regression until each gene is statistically significant in the model.
Cox_Model_filtered <- coxph(formula = Cox_formula_filtered, data = Cox_Matrix)

#Look at results
Cox_Model_filtered %>%
  summary()

Cox_Model_filtered %>%
  tbl_regression(exponentiate = TRUE)

#Create Equivalent to Fig 4B indicating protective and dangerous factors as expression increases for a gene
Cox_Model_filtered %>%
  tidy() %>%
  mutate(group = if_else(estimate > 0, "Dangerous Factor", "Protective Factor")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = -log10(p.value), color = group))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), color = "black", linetype = "dashed")+
  ylim(0,5)+
  xlim(-1,1)+
  labs(x = "coeff")+
  geom_text(aes(label = term),color = "black", nudge_y = 0.25)+
  theme_classic()

#List of 4 Optimized COX Model Terms

COX_OPT_GENE_LIST <- Cox_genes_filtered
```

#Create K-M (Kaplan Meier) Graph showing the overall survival of the model

After the process of systematically in order running a model of all the genes with a statistically significant impact on patient survival with removal of genes. Now, a graph will be created to try to replicate the graph showing 4D

```{r}
#Graph of Data forming a list object with the 4 Genes of Interest

Cox_Matrix %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(COX_OPT_GENE_LIST), barcode, patient_id, days_to_last_follow_up, vital_status, time_in_months, deceased) %>%
  ggadjustedcurves(fit = Cox_Model_filtered,
                   data = .,
                   conf.int = TRUE,
                   fun = "pct")


#Graph Based on the Average that they show
  Cox_Matrix %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(COX_OPT_GENE_LIST), barcode, patient_id, days_to_last_follow_up, vital_status, time_in_months, deceased) %>%
  ggadjustedcurves(fit = Cox_Model_filtered,
                   data = .,
                   conf.int = TRUE,
                   fun = "pct",
                   method = "average")
```
